Subject: Architecture review — proposed times & prep materials

Hi Samir / Emily —

Thanks for committing to an architecture review with our infra/serving team. I booked an initial 60‑minute slot to walk through the proposed integration and to surface any blockers. Can you confirm which of these works for your network & infra folks?

- Tue Jul 7, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed Jul 8, 13:00–14:00 PT
- Thu Jul 9, 09:00–10:00 PT

Attached is a first pass architecture diagram (redwood_arch_v1.pdf) and a calendar invite (calendar_invite.ics). If none of these times work, tell us a few windows and we’ll reschedule.

- expected peak qps & batching targets
- network egress and TLS termination expectations
- data residency & token retention policy
- fallback routing between hosted and dedicated variants

Camila — thanks for the invite. Quick note: the 7/7 morning slot conflicts with our weekly infra sync. Wed 7/8 at 13:00 PT would work better for Samir + our network lead (Lina Park). Can you include Lina? I’ll loop her in once we lock a time.

A couple of items to add to the pre‑read from our side:
- our TLS termination currently is at the edge LB (F5), and we plan to terminate at the LB for now — would Redwood expect mutual TLS to be terminated at the LB or at the application?
- firewall egress ranges: we can provide a CIDR list but need to confirm whether Redwood requires static IPs for allow‑listing.

Thanks Samir — Wed 7/8 13:00 PT works for our infra team. I’ve tentatively added Laura (network infra) and Vivek (runtime) to the invite so we can cover TLS + runtime capacity.

To answer the quick network questions:
- Redwood can support mTLS to the application layer; we also support TLS termination at the edge and re‑encrypt to the runtime if desired. We’ll bring a short slide with supported patterns and tradeoffs.
- We support both static egress IPs (via reserved NAT) and dynamic ranges depending on Dedicated vs Hosted deployment. If you need static allow‑listing, please send the list of destination IPs/ports required and we’ll confirm the exact ranges.

I’ll prepare a brief slide on TLS options and expected port access.

— Dev

I’ll also pull a short slide for the call that shows our expected qps envelope and retention needs.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@northwind.io>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Architecture review — quick answers & pre‑meeting notes

Emily — quick answers ahead of Wed so compliance has something to review: 

- Token retention: default hosted retention is 30 days; Dedicated customers can configure retention policies per contract. We can provide an export workflow or API for redaction on demand.
- Per‑tenant KV encryption: yes — we support customer‑managed keys (KMS) and envelope encryption per tenant for Dedicated deployments. I’ll bring a short slide on key management options and an internal runbook link.
- Static egress IPs: for Dedicated we provide reserved NAT ranges; for hosted we recommend allow‑listing by region and provide a published range set (we can provide exact CIDRs once you share expected endpoints).

Attached is a brief FAQ and the current architecture PDF (redwood_arch_v1.pdf) for the call. We’ll reserve the last 15 minutes for live troubleshooting and detailed firewall/port discussion.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
